title: Premier League Predictions: Chelsea Host Misfiring Man Utd, Arsenal Visit Liverpool in Title Test
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 30, 2026Gabriel was back on the scoresheet for the champions Arsenal last weekend.  / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images There are two headline matches during the peculiarly-scheduled Gameweek 9 of Premier League action.
Manchester United’s trip to Chelsea kicks off a lesser-seen slate of eight games on Halloween this Saturday, with two under-fire managers desperately scrambling for three precious points.

One would anticipate a higher-quality affair when reigning champions Arsenal visit Liverpool in Sunday’s only match, with the in-form Reds providing a significant test of the Gunners’ title-winning credentials.
Elsewhere, there are plenty of other narratives to follow up and down the division, so here are Sports Illustrated’s predictions for Gameweek 9.
Man Utd won both fixtures last season. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesPrediction: Chelsea 2–1 Man Utd

Xabi Alonso is feeling the pressure after some disappointing performances form his Chelsea team this season, but all eyes are on his opposite number in the away dugout at Stamford Bridge this Saturday.

Michael Carrick has been retained for the trip to west London despite Manchester United’s disastrous start to the season, which hit dizzying new lows with back-to-back three-goal defeats to Como and Bournemouth. But the battle with Chelsea feels make-or-break for the 45-year-old.

Having held clear-the-air talks with the dissenting Bruno Fernandes and the rest of his roster, Carrick will hope for a reset against Chelsea. The Red Devils won both meetings last season, including an impressive 1–0 win at Stamford Bridge during Carrick’s interim stint, and can take solace from João Pedro’s continued absence.

The Brazilian is essential for the Blues, as evidenced by defeats to Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur while he’s been sidelined, but Chelsea do at least boast home advantage for a match of fine margins. That could prove the difference between two struggling giants.

Bournemouth supporters must believe they’ve have been living in some kind of utopian simulation over the past over the past five matches. The Cherries have beaten Sturm Graz, AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa 3–0 across three different competitions, while also managing another clean sheet in the 2–0 victory over Sunderland.
It’s a reminder of just how far Bournemouth have come over the past decade, and their winning run could be extended to six matches when Leeds United come to town on Saturday.

The Whites are without victory in four and might simply be overpowered by their in-form hosts, who are really beginning to purr under Marco Rose. A fearsome forward line containing the likes of Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson has just been bolstered by Eli Junior Kroupi’s return, too.
Prediction: Brentford 1–1 Nottingham Forest

Half of the Premier League matches involving Brentford and Nottingham Forest this season have ended in draws. To avoid overthinking their upcoming duel at the Gtech Community Stadium, this one has stalemate written all over it.

Forest certainly need the points more having collected just six from a possible 24 this term—a tally which leaves them in the relegation zone. The Oliver Glasner era is yet to ignite, with goalscoring a familiar issue for the Midlands side.

Brentford, by contrast, sit in sixth despite winning just twice in the league. The draw specialists have managed to steadily climb the standings by simply avoiding defeat, and they should notch at least another point this weekend.

The Premier League’s bottom two lock horns when Sunderland journey to Coventry City for an important encounter. Neither side has impressed early in the campaign, placing even more pressure on the outcome of this one.

Coventry have been brought back down to earth after successive wins, with defeats to Tottenham Hotspur and, more painfully, Fulham leaving them in 19th. They remain an inconsistent beast lacking the star quality to punish establish Premier League sides—for the most part, at least.

Sunderland overperformed last season and are now struggling to juggle European and domestic duties. One would expect them to sort themselves out eventually, but they will be desperate to avoid being cut adrift at the foot of the table.
Unlike fellow promoted side Coventry, it’s been an encouraging start to the campaign for Hull City and Ipswich Town, who have been rewarded for the vast sums splashed over the summer transfer window.
